text:
alice.w: Heads up — PR 7388 landed the adaptive batching tweak and I kicked off a quick canary. Seeing a small regression on long-seq tail latency. Can someone with perf context take a quick look? https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7388 :eyes:

ben.k: saw the deploy-bot message. what numbers are you seeing?

alice.w: quick summary from the canary (r5g 40GB, seq=2048 workloads):
```
before: p95 = 162ms, p99 = 412ms, throughput = 185 req/s, mem per worker = 6.1GB
after:  p95 = 171ms (+5%), p99 = 441ms (+7%), throughput = 178 req/s (-3.8%), mem per worker = 6.9GB (+0.8GB)
```

carmen: that memory bump is suspicious. the batching tweak increases buffer lifetime, right? could be KV cache retain or extra slice allocation per batch.

dmitri: looking at the PR diff now. main change is batching window extension + fallback path. Quick thought: if we extended batch time then average batch size might increase, but for long-seq the KV cache per-request grows -> mem. Also the fallback path allocates a transient tensor with shape [batch, seq, dim].

ben.k: can you paste the microbench command you ran? I'll repro locally.

alice.w: ran the smoke script in infra/bench/run_smoke.sh with FLAGS="--seq 2048 --model redwood-base --concurrency 4 --duration 120s". Full command: `./run_smoke.sh --seq 2048 --concurrency 4 --duration 120s --profile canary-pr-7388`

deploy-bot: Canary deployed: runtime/canary/pr-7388 -> r5g-large (4 workers). Canary logs: https://canary.redwood/dev/7388/logs

carmen: can you grab `top` or `smem` output for one of the worker pids? curious about resident set breakdown.

alice.w: pasted a snippet from `ps` + `smem` on one worker:
```
PID   USER   RSS
10123 alice 6.9G
- python runtime main + native libs: 4.0G
- cuda mapped: 1.6G
- arena/allocs: 800M
```

ben.k: repro'd locally with your flags. I see the p99 bump too but not quite as big (+4%). My machine has slightly different kernel. Running with `--no-adaptive-window` from the PR branch removes regression. So the window extension looks causal.

dmitri: ok, action items:
- revert the adaptive window default to previous value for the canary while we triage (can do config flag)
- instrument the transient tensor allocation path with tagged allocs to confirm origin of +800MB
- add a microbenchmark that exercises KV growth with long sequences to the CI smoke suite

alice.w: +1 on the plan. I can push a config toggle to roll the canary back to the prior window value. Do we need approvals for that change?

carmen: small config change + canary rollback is fine; patch it as a hotfix PR and ping eng-runtime for fast-merge. We should include the bench output in PR description.

ben.k: I'll re-run kv-trace with jemalloc stats on next run and attach logs. If the transient tensor shows up as arena we can mitigate by moving that path to pooled buffers.

alice.w: creating hotfix branch and PR now (link when ready). expectation: rollback + added debug alloc tags. If we get a clean canary (<2% regression) we can then iterate on improving the window algorithm.

dmitri: ping me when PR is up, I'll review first. Also include a short note for SRE about the canary state so they don't escalate prematurely.

deploy-bot: Deploy note: Canary pr-7388 rolled to config:adaptive_window=old -> will start after 2m. Monitor: #incidents (auto), perf-dashboard/pr-7388.

alice.w: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7391 — includes rollback config + alloc-tagging. Requesting 2x fast approvals. cc @dmitri @ben.k @carmen

ben.k: quick review passed. left a minor comment about log verbosity.

carmen: approved, left nits.

dmitri: approved, will merge after CI passes. make sure to squash the debug commit before GA.

alice.w: thanks all. will follow up with updated canary numbers in ~15m. :thumbsup:
